How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide you can copy into your own scripts or Postman/Insomnia collections.  
It shows **how to build** a *REST* request against the **Cisco Nexus Dashboard v6.3.1** service that returns “Device Connector Versions” – i.e., all firmware/software releases available for each type of connector (USB, Ethernet, etc.).

> ⚠️ Replace placeholders (`<…>` ) with values specific to your environment before running.

---

## 1️⃣ Prerequisites  

| Item | What it means |
|------|---------------|
| `BASE_URL` | HTTPS address of the Nexus Dashboard instance (e.g. `https://nexus.example.com`) |
| `TOKEN`   | OAuth/JWT bearer token obtained through the login flow (`POST /login`, `/oauth/token`, …) |
| `DEVICE_ID` *(optional)* | If you only care about one particular device’s connectors |

If you don’t have a token yet:

```bash
curl -k \
  -X POST https://nexus.example.com/api/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"admin","password":"P@ssw0rd"}'
```

Response will contain `"access_token": "<JWT>"`. Copy that value → `TOKEN`.

---

## 2️⃣ Endpoint Overview  

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/api/v2/deviceconnectorversions` | Returns list of all supported connector version objects. |
| `GET` | `/api/v2/devices/{deviceId}/connectors` | Returns connector info for a single device (if you supply `{deviceId}`). |

For this tutorial we’ll hit the first endpoint because it gives the full catalog.

### Full URL Example

```
https://nexus.example.com/api/v2/deviceconnectorversions
```

Add optional query strings such as `page=1&size=50` if pagination is required.

---

## 3️⃣ Sample Requests  

### A. cURL (Command Line)

```bash
curl -k \
  -X GET "https://nexus.example.com/api/v2/deviceconnectorversions?page=1&size=100" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"
```

#### Expected Response Skeleton

```json
[
  {
    "id": "dcv-12345",
    "name": "Ethernet 10G Base-T",
    "firmware_version": "5.7.12",
    "release_date": "2024-01-15T00:00:00Z",
    "supported_devices": ["NXOS", "IOS-XE"],
    ...
  },
  …
]
```

### B. Python (requests lib)

```python
import os
import json
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://nexus.example.com"
ENDPOINT = "/api/v2/deviceconnectorversions"

headers = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.getenv('TOKEN')}",
    "Accept": "application/json",
}

payload = {"page": 1, "size": 200}
resp = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}{ENDPOINT}", headers=headers, params=payload, verify=False)
resp.raise_for_status()

data = resp.json()
print(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
```

> 👉 Set `verify=True` when you’re sure the server has a valid cert.

### C. PowerShell (Invoke-RestMethod)

```powershell
$baseUrl = "https://nexus.example.com"
$endpoint = "/api/v2/deviceconnectorversions"
$uri = "$baseUrl$endpoint?page=1&size=100"

$response = Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri $uri `
  -Headers @{ 
      Authorization="Bearer $env:TOKEN";
      Accept="application/json"
  } `
  -UseBasicParsing

$response # prints array of connector-version objects
```

---

## 4️⃣ Common Pitfalls & Tips  

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **401 Unauthorized** | Verify that `$TOKEN` hasn’t expired. Re‑run the login step. |
| **SSL verification error** | Either set `--insecure/-k` flag in cURL, `verify=False` in Python, or install proper CA bundle. |
| **Empty result set** | Check whether you need to specify filters (`status=open`, `family=ethernet`). |
| **Pagination** | Default page size may be limited (~20 items). Add `page=` and/or `size=` query args. |
| **Rate limiting** | Respect `Retry-After` header if returned. |

---

## 5️⃣ Quick Reference Cheat Sheet  

| Action | Command Snippet |
|--------|-----------------|
| Get auth token | See section 1 |
| List all connector versions | `GET /api/v2/deviceconnectorversions` |
| Filter by family | `GET /api/v2/deviceconnectorversions?family=usb` |
| Pagination | Append `?page=<num>&size=<count>` |
| Single device connectors | `GET /api/v2/devices/<ID>/connectors` |

Feel free to paste the snippets above directly into your favorite IDE or terminal window—just replace `<...>` tokens with real values. Happy automating!
